title: The Lenox Club breakfast dance where Armstrong threw Rex Stewart's horn away
summary: After Armstrong's Savoy appearance, musicians jammed at the Lenox Club's Sunday breakfast dances, and Armstrong outplayed Rex Stewart and Jack Teagarden.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You know, my stories are long because I pause for a long time between words...
Anyway, let's get to the Lenox Club.

The Lenox Club was a nice little nightclub, an intimate spot in Harlem in the Roarin' Twenties. It used to be the home of... Well, I don't know. But it was a nice little place. It was not a big place. It was a small place, a small club.

Yeah, they used to have breakfast dances there. They would start at twelve o'clock Sunday night, and they'd run all night long, until the last couple go out, which was six-seven o'clock in the morning sometimes.

Anyway, Louis made his appearance at the Savoy, which was one block down the street from this place. And after he finished at the Savoy, everybody went... Not everybody, because everybody couldn't get in that little club. They went to... The musicians went to the Lenox Club, to sit and jam and one-thing-and-another. And Rex Stewart happened to be there, and oh, he was blowin' his head off. I think, I'm not certain...yeah, Jack Teagarden was also there. Yes, he was there that morning, too. He was on the stand playing. Rex Stewart, and Rex was playing with his little trumpet -- and he could blow. Rex could really play.
They all played. All of them that thought they could play. Everybody had their chance.

And then Louis got up there and played... Threw Rex Stewart's horn away. Heh-heh. Rex was laughin'! Threw his horn away. He had never heard nothin' like Louis in his life. Louis was exciting. He was something to hear, you know! But...
